newsitem.title: UK: Angerstein profits up on insurance profits.
newsitem.headline: Angerstein profits up on insurance profits.

text.p: Angerstein Underwriting Trust Plc said on Wednesday its pre-tax profits for the year to May 31 were boosted by the first contribution from Lloyd's of London insurance business.

The company, one of the first wave of corporate investors in the insurance market, reported pre-tax profits of 21.7 million stg versus 3.7 million last time and earnings per share of 12.6 pence versus 2.8.
The profits included 17.4 million stg from the 1994 underwriting year, the first year Angerstein invested in the Lloyd's market, which reports results three years in arrears.
This represents an 8.4 percent return on the 207.8 million stg capacity Angerstein had in Lloyd's in 1994. The dividend for the year was increased to 10.2 pence from 2.8.
Angerstein said the outlook for the 1995 and 1996 years at Lloyd's was encouraging, but was less positive about 1997 and 1998.
"Although no major losses have not yet been incurred in the 1997 account, the windstorm season is not over and rates have deteriorated," it said in a statement.
Consequently, Angerstein is reviewing its Lloyd's investments with a view to concentrating on fewer insurance syndicates, which it considers better able to weather difficult market conditions.
Its current estimate for the 1995 year is for an underwriting return of between 6.1 and 10.7 percent after all fees and commissions.
